easy.def: To put things in a bag or box.
examples: Pack your bag.
We packed for the trip.
He packs his lunch.

more.def: To put things into a bag, box or suitcase to carry them.
examples: I packed my swimsuit and towel in a bag.
Dad packs our lunches every morning.
We packed the car for the trip.

easy.def: A group of wolves or dogs.
examples: A pack of wolves howled.
The pack ran through the snow.
A pack of dogs barked.

more.def: A group of animals, such as wolves or dogs, that live or hunt together.
examples: A pack of wolves traveled across the snowy plain.
The pack of dogs ran along the beach.
Each pack of wolves has a leader.

easy.def: A small box or bag of things.
examples: I bought a pack of gum.
She opened a pack of cards.
We need a pack of pencils.

more.def: A small package that holds several of the same thing.
examples: She bought a pack of pencils for school.
A pack of cards has fifty-two cards.
Mom opened a new pack of napkins.

easy.def: A hurting feeling.
examples: I feel pain in my knee.
The shot caused a little pain.
He cried out in pain.

more.def: A feeling of hurt in the body.
examples: I felt a sharp pain in my foot.
The medicine took away the pain.
She had a pain in her tooth.

easy.def: A friend.
examples: He is my pal.
My pal and I play ball.
She is a good pal.

more.def: A close and friendly companion.
examples: My pal and I walk to school together.
He is a loyal pal who always helps.
She wrote to her pen pal.

easy.def: Clothes that cover both legs.
examples: I wear pants to school.
My pants are blue.
Put on your pants.

more.def: A piece of clothing that covers the body from the waist to the ankles, with a separate part for each leg.
examples: He wore warm pants in the snow.
My pants have deep pockets.
She rolled up her pants to wade in the creek.

easy.def: Thin, flat sheets for writing and drawing.
examples: I draw pictures on paper.
Fold the paper in half.
We recycle old paper.

more.def: Thin, flat material made from wood or plants, used for writing, printing and wrapping.
examples: Paper is made from wood that is crushed and pressed flat.
She folded a sheet of paper into a bird.
Put the used paper in the recycling bin.

easy.def: A newspaper.
examples: Dad reads the paper.
The paper came this morning.
The paper had a picture of our school.

more.def: A set of printed pages of news that comes out each day or week.
examples: Grandpa reads the paper while he drinks his tea.
The local paper wrote about our school fair.
Our neighbor delivers the paper every morning.

easy.def: A polite word to say you are sorry.
examples: Pardon me, I did not hear you.
Pardon? Can you say it again?
Pardon me for bumping you.

more.def: A polite way to say sorry, or to ask someone to say something again.
examples: Pardon me, may I pass?
Pardon? I did not catch your name.
Pardon me for being late.

easy.def: To forgive someone.
examples: Please pardon me.
The king pardoned the boy.
Pardon my mess.

more.def: To forgive someone or to let them go without punishment.
examples: The king pardoned the prisoner.
Please pardon the mess in my room.
The governor pardoned the man.

easy.def: A mother or father.
examples: My parent drives me to school.
Both parents came to the show.
Ask your parent first.

more.def: A mother or father, or someone who takes care of a child as they would.
examples: Each parent signed the permission slip.
The parent bird brought worms to its chicks.
A parent or guardian must come with young swimmers.

easy.def: A place outside with grass and trees to play.
examples: We play at the park.
The park has swings.
Let's go to the park.

more.def: A public place with grass, trees and often playgrounds, where people go to play and relax.
examples: We had a picnic in the park.
The park has a pond with ducks.
Kids play soccer at the park.

easy.def: To leave a car in a place.
examples: Dad parked the car.
We park here.
Please park by the tree.

more.def: To stop a vehicle and leave it in a place for a while.
examples: Dad parked the car in front of the library.
You may not park by the fire hydrant.
We parked near the beach.

easy.def: A piece of something bigger.
examples: This is part of the toy.
Eat a part of the pie.
Tell me the best part.

more.def: A piece or section of something larger.
examples: The wheel is one part of the bicycle.
Which part of the story did you like best?
He ate a small part of the cake and saved the rest.

easy.def: A person you do something with.
examples: My partner and I did the project.
Find a partner for the game.
She is my dance partner.

more.def: A person who does an activity or works together with you.
examples: My science partner and I built a volcano.
Each dancer has a partner.
Choose a partner and sit together.

easy.def: A time when people get together to have fun.
examples: I went to a party.
It is her birthday party.
We had a party.

more.def: A gathering where people enjoy themselves with food, games, or music.
examples: We had a birthday party with games and a big cake.
The class held a party at the end of the year.
My neighbors invited everyone to a block party.

easy.def: To go past something.
examples: Cars pass our house all day.
We passed the park on the way.
A butterfly passed by my nose.

more.def: To go by or move past something without stopping.
examples: The train passed through the small town without slowing down.
We passed three farms before we reached the lake.
Please let the ambulance pass.

easy.def: To hand something to someone.
examples: Please pass the salt.
He passed me the ball.
Pass the book to Mia.

more.def: To give something to another person by hand or by throwing it.
examples: Could you pass the bread down to the end of the table?
The player passed the ball to her teammate near the goal.
The note was passed from desk to desk.

easy.def: To do well enough on a test.
examples: I passed my spelling test.
Did you pass the quiz?
She will pass her swimming test.

more.def: To do well enough on a test to move on to the next step.
examples: He studied hard so he would pass the math test.
Everyone in the class passed the reading quiz.
She passed her swimming test and earned a new badge.

easy.def: Time that is over.
examples: In the past, people rode horses.
My grandpa tells stories about the past.
We read about the past.

more.def: The time before now.
examples: In the past, people wrote letters by hand.
Grandpa told us stories about the past.
Museums teach us about the past.

easy.def: Going by something.
examples: Walk past the school.
The car drove past our house.
Go past the park.

more.def: Farther than, or on the other side of something.
examples: Go past the bakery and turn left.
The bus drove past our house without stopping.
She ran past the finish line.

easy.def: Able to wait without getting upset.
examples: Be patient. It will be your turn soon.
The patient dog waited for its food.
Be patient while the cake bakes.

more.def: Able to stay calm while waiting or when something is hard.
examples: The patient teacher explained the problem again until everyone understood.
You must be patient when you are fishing.
She is patient with her little brother when he learns new games.

easy.def: Shapes, colors, or things that repeat again and again.
examples: My shirt has a pattern of red and blue dots.
The rug has a pattern of stars.
Clap the pattern with me.

more.def: A design or set of things that repeats in a regular way.
examples: Can you find the pattern in these numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8?
The tiles made a pattern of blue and white squares.
Scientists look for patterns in the weather.

easy.def: To give money for something.
examples: I pay for the toy.
Dad paid the bill.
She pays with coins.

more.def: To give money in return for something you buy or for work that was done.
examples: We paid for our tickets at the door.
The bakery pays its workers every Friday.
I used my savings to pay for the new bike.
